overview:
The target result is a deterministic [fixed-tape machine](fixed-tape-model.md) that multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, for a fixed $\kappa = 2^{-182}$. It disproves the [Schonhage-Strassen optimality conjecture](schonhage-strassen-conjecture.md), which asserts that $n\log n$ is the best order of growth for multiplication in this model. The gain is a [power saving](power-saving.md) in the logarithmic factor, a polynomial saving in $\lg n$ rather than a change to the leading term.

The route runs through seven parts. The first fixes the model and the conjecture. The second builds a [linear network](linear-network.md) with [sources and sinks](network-terminal.md) and [frames](frame.md) that fix how each array is stored, together with [role streams](role-streams.md) and the [address shear](address-shear.md). The third adds [subset-intersection networks](subset-network.md), [nested subspace labels](subspace-labels.md) and the [rank-saving recursion](recursive-saving.md), which gives the saving. The fourth sets up [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md), the [Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md), [tensor products](tensor-product.md), [roots of unity](roots-of-unity.md), the [polynomial ring](polynomial-ring.md) and the [quotient ring](quotient-ring.md). The fifth reduces integer multiplication to convolution through [radix digits](radix-digit-convolution.md) and a [Chinese-remainder axis map](crt-axis-map.md), then rewrites the transforms by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) and [Bluestein's identity](bluestein.md). The sixth computes packed polynomial products with [butterfly layers](butterfly-layer.md), [synthetic transforms](synthetic-transform.md) and [signed packing](signed-packing.md), and recovers exact coefficients by [rounding and carries](exact-recovery.md). The last part adds the [fast interchange of address chunks](tape-interchange.md) and assembles the [fixed-tape multiplier](fixed-tape-multiplication.md).

parts.title: Model and conjecture
parts.intro: The target is a bound against a conjecture about the best growth rate in this model, so the reader needs the [fixed-tape machine](fixed-tape-model.md) and the [Schonhage-Strassen conjecture](schonhage-strassen-conjecture.md). [Power saving](power-saving.md) names the form of improvement sought, a bound $n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa}$ smaller than $n\log n$ by a polynomial factor in $\lg n$. The [established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier](multiplier-subroutine.md) is the black-box subroutine the construction calls on shorter integers.

parts.title: Linear networks and frames
parts.intro: The construction moves values between two banks through a fixed [linear network](linear-network.md), whose wires end at [sources and sinks](network-terminal.md). A [frame](frame.md) at each vertex records how the array on each wire is stored, so frame changes cancel between the two ends of a route. [Role streams](role-streams.md) and the [address shear](address-shear.md) give the concrete storage layout that the later parts rely on.

parts.title: Rank-saving recursion
parts.intro: This part gives the combinatorial core. [Subset-intersection networks](subset-network.md) realise the scalar exchange of two banks by intersection sizes, and [nested subspace labels](subspace-labels.md) bound the work on each edge by dimension drops. The [rank-saving recursion](recursive-saving.md) turns these bounds into a cost that grows by less than $m$ when the parameter grows by $m$, which is the source of the saving.

parts.title: Transforms and polynomial rings
parts.intro: Multiplication is reduced to convolution and transforms, so the reader needs [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) and the [discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) first. [Tensor products](tensor-product.md) and [multidimensional transforms](multidim-transform.md) express one-dimensional operations on several coordinates as a single operation. [Roots of unity](roots-of-unity.md) in the [polynomial ring](polynomial-ring.md) and its [quotient by several relations](quotient-ring.md) supply the algebra used by the Chinese-remainder step.

parts.title: Reduction to cyclic convolution
parts.intro: Each $n$-bit input is split into [radix digits](radix-digit-convolution.md), so that multiplication becomes a convolution with small coefficients. The [Chinese-remainder axis map](crt-axis-map.md) places these coefficients on pairwise coprime cyclic axes, turning one cyclic convolution into a multidimensional one. [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) and [Bluestein's identity](bluestein.md) then rewrite the prime-length transforms as normalized cyclic convolutions.

parts.title: Packed polynomial convolution
parts.intro: The normalized convolution is computed over $\mathbb{C}[y]/(y^r+1)$ by [butterfly layers](butterfly-layer.md) and [synthetic transforms](synthetic-transform.md), in which twiddle multiplications become signed shifts. [Signed coefficient packing](signed-packing.md) turns the polynomial products into integer products. [Exact recovery](exact-recovery.md) rounds the computed values, whose error is below $1/2$, and then propagates carries to give the binary product.

parts.title: Assembling the multiplier
parts.intro: The procedure must permute stored addresses cheaply, which the [fast interchange of address chunks](tape-interchange.md) does in time $O(V u^{\tau})$ for a fixed $\tau<1$. The [fixed-tape multiplier](fixed-tape-multiplication.md) combines the earlier parts into the main theorem, with $\kappa=2^{-182}$ and worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$.
